newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wood Gundy to buy Australia's Eyres Reed.
newsitem.headline: Wood Gundy to buy Australia's Eyres Reed.

text.p: Canadian financial services group CIBC Wood Gundy, a subsidiary of the Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, will acquire 100 percent of Australian stockbroker Eyres Reed Ltd, both companies said on Friday.
The acquisition, agreed with the principals of Eyres Reed, is subject to regulatory approvals, they said in a joint statement.

Eyres Reed, a member firm of the Australian Stock Exchange, is a full-service brokerage firm specialising in resource company shares, particularly in mining and related industries, the statement said.
The firm, which traces its history back to 1896, is the only stockbroker with an office in Kalgoorlie, the mining centre of Western Australia, it said.

Western Australia is Australia's leading mining state, producing some 75 percent of Australia's annual gold production which has grown to 289 tonnes in 1996 from 17 tonnes in 1980, the statement said.
"Eyres Reed sought an alliance that would give clients thorough access to an international information and product network," Eyres Reed chairman David Reed said.

"Now we can remain a strong regional brokerage firm while levering off CIBC Wood Gundy's international network to provide capital raising, underwriting agreements and corporate advice," Reed said in the statement.
Sydney-based Don Lindsay, a managing director in CIBC Wood Gundy's global mining operations, said: "A strong presence in Australia is crucial to being a global player in mining."
Eyres Reed produces the Eyres Reed Explorers Index of junior mining shares and the Eyres Reed Gold Book and is a senior sponsor and chair of the annual Diggers and Dealers gold forum in Kalgoorlie.
Eyre Reed's activities and staff will be integrated with those of CIBC Wood Gundy's Australian subsidiary.

The merged group's institutional and investment banking activities will be carried out under the banner of CIBC Wood Gundy Australia while retail broking and funds management will carry on business under the Eyres Reed name, the statement said.
